hero.tagline: An impressionist journey through light, philosophy & the cosmos

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: The Moon controls the tides of the ocean and the tides of the mind. In Vedic thought, Chandra governs the Manas — the emotional mind — and its phases mirror the cycles of human desire and detachment.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: Nietzsche warned that 'whoever fights monsters should see to it that in the process he does not become a monster.' The ego, in its quest to prove its strength, often becomes the very thing it opposes.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: Krishna describes three paths to liberation: Karma Yoga (selfless action), Jnana Yoga (knowledge), and Bhakti Yoga (devotion). The Gita does not prescribe one path — it honors all three as valid ways to the divine.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: Shiva is called Tryambaka — the three-eyed one. The third eye represents the eye of wisdom that sees beyond the duality of good and evil, self and other, creation and destruction. When it opens, the universe is consumed in flame — not as punishment, but as liberation.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: Art is not what you see, but what you make others see. The painter does not copy the world — they translate it, filtering reality through the lens of emotion, memory, and dream.
